questions.q: True or false? Our centre back should leave their runner to help the left back.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. The centre back keeps their mark, and a spare outlet helps short.
choiceExplanations: Leaving the runner frees a blue player in the middle. A spare outlet helps instead.
Right, it's false. The centre back keeps their mark, and a spare outlet helps short.

questions.q: Blue plays two players short. Which picture helps short and keeps all three runners marked?
options: Left back alone at the corner
questions.explain: Right. The nearer outlet helps short, and all three central runners stay marked.
choiceExplanations: The left back faces two players alone, so blue can pass around them.
The centre back left their runner, so a blue player is free in front of our goal.
Right. The nearer outlet helps short, and all three central runners stay marked.

questions.q: Now a blue player marks our nearer winger. Which release should the keeper use?
options: Short pass to the right winger
questions.explain: Right. We keep two release heights, so when one is marked the higher one is free.
choiceExplanations: A blue player stands right next to that winger, so the pass could be stolen.
Right. We keep two release heights, so when one is marked the higher one is free.
A blue striker stands in that short lane, so the pass could be stolen near our goal.

questions.q: The keeper holds the ball and the nearer winger is open. Which release keeps it safest?
options: Punt it high down the middle
Roll it out to the winger
questions.explain: Yes. A roll-out along the ground is quick and easy to control, so we keep the ball.
choiceExplanations: A high punt is a 50-50 ball that the other team can win.
Waiting lets their players mark the winger and press the keeper.
Yes. A roll-out along the ground is quick and easy to control, so we keep the ball.
